nonBlocking: Compile fix is sound: @MainActor on runCommandTimelineGates() matches the isolation of the global check/checkEqual helpers and counters; call site in main.swift top-level code is already MainActor. No assertion or runtime change. tests.log confirms 2094/0 on the real device.

Driver gates are correctly ordered and strict: serial reference IDs vs frozen baseline (fatalError), OFF and ON arm IDs vs serial, full 262144 finite logits at all 32 outputs, worst rel < 1e-4 vs serial and ON vs OFF, trace validity (eventCount>0, valid==count, no rejections, not truncated, no missing sequence, no skipped gap pairs). The frozenBaselineIDsMatch/instrumentationIDsMatch fields are literal true; acceptable only because the guards precede them, but the doc should say they are guard-implied, not computed fields.

Toggle worst of exactly 0 on all three fixtures means ON vs OFF logits were bit-identical, which is the right evidence that the hooks do not alter dispatch or math. Serial-vs-prepared worst 7.5e-5 on raw-hello is 75% of the 1e-4 gate; report it as margin, not as 'comfortably passing'.

Aggregate consistency: gpuMsPerStep + commitToGPUStartMsPerStep + GPUEndToNextCommitMsPerStep reproduces diagnosticWallMsPerStep within 0.03 ms on all fixtures (78.70/78.72, 81.19/81.22, 82.69/82.71). The doc must state that GPUEndToWaitReturn and encode are overlapping sub-intervals of that decomposition and must not be added to it.

Wall per step includes the full-vocabulary logits readback (262144 floats, ~1 MB) and Output storage inside executeGraphContinue timing, plus loop overhead. The step-boundary gap is therefore a driver artifact; maxGapMs (5.6-7.9 ms) versus ~10-12 ms total gap per step over 37 commands is consistent with one large boundary gap and small intra-step gaps. State explicitly that intra-step submission gaps, not the boundary gap, are the only part relevant to a kernel-shape or hardware candidate discussion.

Paging: globalPagingDeltas show ~229k swapins and ~206k swapouts over the 125 s run, i.e. several GB of swap traffic during decode. The timing gaps in this trace were captured under memory pressure. The doc must say any bottleneck classification from this trace is provisional and should be re-derived from a run with near-zero swap deltas before being used as a hardware candidate list. This does not affect the numerical or ID gates.

diagnostic-summary.json fields (kernelsPerToken 1349.0, per-step ms aggregates, gpuPercentOfWall) are not emitted by diagnose.swift; they are post-hoc derivations from the Report trace. The doc must name the derivation step and state whether gpuMsPerStep comes from trace GPU start/end intervals or from steps[].gpuSeconds (x.gpuMicros); both exist and could differ. kernelsPerToken (1349 vs 37 command buffers per step) needs its source stated since the trace alone does not record kernels per command buffer.
No OFF-arm wall timing is recorded (tracedSteps only when enabled), so the hooks' own wall overhead is unmeasured. The summary makes no claim about it, which is correct; do not add one.
protocol.json lists pmset thermal/battery telemetry but the summary reports only vm_stat deltas; either include them or state they were omitted.

Terminology for the English report: 'gpuPercentOfWall' is GPU command-elapsed share of diagnostic wall, not utilization, occupancy or bandwidth; 'commitToGPUStart' is observed submission latency; 'GPUEndToNextCommit' is observed host submission gap including driver output storage. Keep the existing failed A/A controls (40.46%/23.81% vs 5% gate) stated as unchanged so no throughput or gain language appears. Runtime hooks may be promoted only as default-off diagnostics; no optimized pass is activated and no persisted production artifact is rewritten.
rationale: Source and library are byte-identical to the previously accepted review; the only change is a test-target isolation annotation that fixed a build error without touching assertions or runtime, and the full 2094-check suite passed on the real M1 Max. The independent driver uses a fresh public verification install of E4/R32 and Q4 width 32 against the historical cached model digest, not a retagged gold artifact, and its gates (frozen-baseline ID equality, exact OFF/ON/serial ID equality, finite full-vocabulary logits at every one of 32 outputs, 1e-4 relative bound) all passed with ON-vs-OFF bit-identical. The trace is complete and valid for all three fixtures and its aggregates are internally consistent with the measured wall. Remaining items are documentation and interpretation requirements: overlapping metrics, driver-induced boundary gap, heavy swap activity during the run, and provenance of post-hoc summary fields. None change the correctness or safety of the opt-in timeline, none support a performance claim, and the prior A/A failure remains the governing floor for any future gain qualification.
